principle_text: When the persuadee shares personal information without indicating increased engagement, avoid assuming that sharing similar details alone will advance their willingness to donate.
When the persuadee shares personal and emotional information, avoid focusing solely on unrelated small talk that does not connect back to the charitable cause or donation goal.
When the persuadee shares detailed personal challenges, avoid focusing solely on empathy without connecting the conversation to the charitable cause or donation goal.
When the persuadee shares personal challenges and rewards related to caring for loved ones, you should express empathy and acknowledge their experience to build rapport and openness.
When the persuadee shares personal stories related to caregiving or family, avoid making generic compliments that do not advance the donation conversation or connect to the charitable cause.
When the persuadee shows positive engagement with personal stories but the topic drifts from the donation goal, avoid sharing unrelated details that do not advance the charitable cause.
When the persuadee shares personal pride in their family without connecting to the charitable cause, avoid focusing on unrelated personal achievements that do not advance the donation goal.
When the persuadee shares personal stories related to children, you should connect those stories to the charitable cause and make a clear, direct donation request.
When a persuadee agrees to donate a specific amount, you should confirm the amount and the method of donation clearly to secure their commitment and make the process easy.
When the persuadee responds positively but without reinforcing the donation commitment, avoid making only general compliments that do not further encourage or confirm the charitable action.
When the persuadee has just agreed to donate and expressed positive feelings, avoid abruptly ending the conversation without expressing appreciation to maintain goodwill and a positive relationship.
